prompt: Name a Pixar feature film with a one-word title.
label: Easy Opener
note: Verified against a current list of Pixar's theatrical features (Oct 2026): thirteen one-word titles, including Elio (released June 2025) and Hoppers (released March 2026, the newest at the time of writing). A later release extends the list rather than breaking it — add it here the same way, don't wait for a full review pass.

answers.name: Cars
answers.fact: 2006. Radiator Springs is modeled on real Route 66 towns bypassed by the interstate.

answers.name: Up
answers.fact: 2009. The opening montage of Carl and Ellie's marriage runs under four minutes and is one of the most-cited tearjerkers in film.

answers.name: WALL-E
answers.fact: 2008. The first act runs almost without dialogue — a bet that the story alone could carry a children's film.

answers.name: Coco
answers.fact: 2017. Built around Dia de los Muertos, with a standing council of Mexican and Mexican-American cultural consultants.

answers.name: Brave
answers.fact: 2012. Pixar's first film with a solo female lead, and its first set in a real historical backdrop.

answers.name: Ratatouille
answers.fact: 2007. The crew animated a working 'taste map' to track every ingredient Remy could smell on screen.

answers.name: Soul
answers.fact: 2020. Released straight to streaming during the pandemic — Pixar's first film to skip a theatrical debut.

answers.name: Luca
answers.fact: 2021. Set on the Italian Riviera; the sea monsters' true forms only ever show once they're wet.

answers.name: Lightyear
answers.fact: 2022. Framed in-universe as the film Andy's toy was modeled on, rather than the other way around.

answers.name: Onward
answers.fact: 2020. A half-worked resurrection spell leaves its two leads as mostly just a pair of legs for most of the runtime.

answers.name: Elemental
answers.fact: 2023. Opened soft, then turned into a sleeper hit through word of mouth over the summer.

answers.name: Elio
answers.fact: 2025. Pixar's first film centered on a human child's first contact with an actual alien civilization.

answers.name: Hoppers
answers.fact: 2026. A college student transfers her mind into a robotic beaver to live among the wildlife she's trying to save.

distractors.name: Toy Story
distractors.note: A real Pixar film, but a three-word title — this round only counts one-word ones.

distractors.name: Toy Story 2
distractors.note: A real sequel, and still three words.

distractors.name: Toy Story 3
distractors.note: Still three words, same as the first two.

distractors.name: Toy Story 4
distractors.note: The fourth one doesn't shrink the title any more than the first three did.

distractors.name: Finding Nemo
distractors.note: A real Pixar film, just two words — not a one-word title.

distractors.name: The Incredibles
distractors.note: Two words plus an article — a real Pixar film all the same, just not a one-word title.

distractors.name: Monsters Inc
distractors.note: Two words — 'Inc' doesn't make it a one-word title.

distractors.name: Inside Out
distractors.note: Two real words, just not one of them.

distractors.name: Turning Red
distractors.note: A real, recent Pixar film — two words, not one.

distractors.name: A Bug's Life
distractors.note: Three words — one of Pixar's very first films, still not one-word.

distractors.name: Finding Dory
distractors.note: Finding Nemo's sequel, and just as many words.

distractors.name: Frozen
distractors.note: Disney Animation, not Pixar — a different studio under the same corporate roof.

distractors.name: Moana
distractors.note: Also Disney Animation, not Pixar — one of the most common mix-ups between the two studios.
